correctness.rationale: The scoped corner-start survival theorem is correct, but the frozen Finding makes a literally false size statement: the distance-two shell contains binom(d,2) vertices, not exponentially many. Its unqualified phrase 'removes every dark component' cannot hold outside the corner-accessible sector; in d=6 the tensor (|01⟩−|10⟩)⊗3 is supported entirely on shell three, and adjacency annihilates each pair factor, so it is an exact dark full-space eigenstate with both first and second shells monitored. The body correctly confines the two-shell proof to radial states. There the normalized Walsh sum at energy d−2k has corner weight binom(d,k)/2^d and shell overlap proportional to K_r(k;d). A real eigenvalue of the dissipative operator requires zero loss expectation, hence a dark adjacency eigenvector. Its span reduces the operator and every other radial spectral value has strictly negative imaginary part, which implies decay even with Jordan blocks. The quadratic identity gives square dimensions with integral k=(d±sqrt(d))/2 and the stated weights, including d=4,9,16; r=0,d have no zeros and γ>0 is necessary for the decay argument. Stirling at one standard deviation gives the stated prefactor. The failed disposition would stand on originality even if both scope and size wording were corrected.
correctness.replay: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 /workspace/branches/frozen_replay.py 3 constructs full signed Walsh shell restrictions (not a radial tridiagonal diagonalization), numerically projects onto each energy-sector kernel for all radii and the pair (1,2), and compares to exact rational corner weights for d=2..9 (tolerance 1e−10). It also checks the d=6 nonradial witness by exact vertex sums. The frozen script was inspected but not executed.

originality.rationale: The distinct same-day indexed all-shell harmonic-restriction theorem covers the substantive results, even though it does not print the particular square-dimension fraction. It treats the same Hamiltonian with more general positive site losses and gives the entire shell restriction on each harmonic summand. Its i=0 block is precisely the corner-relevant block; both the r=2 classification and the shells-1-plus-2 statement are direct polynomial specializations. This is demonstrable coverage, not a claim of which record was first.
residual_risks: No priority ordering can be inferred between distinct same-day records. The bounded search does not decide whether an even earlier source stated the square case; the verified stronger indexed comparison already decides coverage.

value.rationale: Exact shell absorption on hypercubes is a worthwhile problem, but in the presence of the verified all-shell restriction the claimed contribution reduces to its trivial-harmonic summand, a quadratic zero calculation and the intersection of two scalar kernels. The exact fractions and the standard Stirling estimate do not provide a further independent contribution. The nonradial witness diagnoses a scope issue rather than rescuing the already-covered corner theorem.
